validity.researcher_notes: SOLE SUPPORT IS ONE ORIGIN, NOW ROTTED. The gem.wiki row cites only OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletin 2012 (p.75) and ASB2013 (p.79) — two editions of the SAME OPEC publication, i.e. one origin, not two independent sources. Both URLs now 403 (opec.org retired the old flipbook/static paths; url_verifier FAIL on the ASB2013 flipbook page). No independent source names a discrete '40-inch, ~193 km Safaniyah–Ju'aymah gas pipeline'. GulfPub PE World Map — Saudi Arabia is its best-covered gas country (20 features) — has NO Safaniya gas line at all (its Safaniya-area gas is captured only via the offshore-gathering / Master Gas System narrative). CORROBORATION FOR THE FLOW, NOT THE LINE: Fluor's Aramco Offshore Gas Gathering project (independent, verified 200) states Safaniya/Marjan/Zuluf field gas is gathered and taken to shore, then moved along the coast to Berri, Shedgum and Ju'aymah for processing — so gas does move from the Safaniya area toward Ju'aymah, but as '>150 miles of various-diameter, primarily offshore' gathering pipe, not a single named 193 km trunk. NOTE A SAME-CORRIDOR TWIN: GEM also carries 'Safaniyah-Juaymah oil pipeline' (198 km, 46/48 in, operating) citing the identical OPEC ASB 2012 p.75. The two rows share source, endpoints and (on the sheet) length; the gas row is plausibly a distinct OPEC ASB gas line-item (different 40 in / 193 km specs) but cannot be independently validated. Verdict: real gas transport corridor, unconfirmed as a discrete named transmission line.

validity.researcher_notes: SHEET LENGTH LOOKS COPIED FROM THE OIL TWIN. Sheet LengthKnown=198.00 km, but GEM's own gem.wiki page for THIS gas line states 193 km/123 mi and 40 in. 198 km is exactly the length of the separate 'Safaniyah-Juaymah oil pipeline' (198 km, 46/48 in) — strong sign the oil line's 198 km was carried onto the gas row while the underlying OPEC figure for the gas line is 193 km. Diameter 40 in is supported only by OPEC ASB (single, now-dead origin); no independent corroboration found. Capacity blank and unsourceable (Fluor gives 170 MMSCFD for Safaniya FIELD gathering, not for a Ju'aymah trunk). No >=2 independent agreement on any spec → spec concern, not a silent pass.

routes.start_name: Safaniya field / onshore Safaniya gas-gathering facilities (Eastern Province Gulf coast, near Tanajib/Manifa)
routes.end_name: Ju'aymah terminal / gas-processing facilities (near Ras Tanura)
routes.corridor_desc: Runs south-southeast down the Eastern Province Arabian Gulf coast from the Safaniya field/onshore Safaniya facilities (~28.0N, ~48.77E; Safaniya field is ~260 km north of Dhahran per nsenergybusiness), passing the Manifa/Jubail coastal stretch, to the Ju'aymah terminal near Ras Tanura (~26.88N, ~49.93E). This is a LOOSE corridor: endpoints are named/defensible from well-documented places, but the true start point (offshore field vs onshore Safaniya GOSP-1) and whether routing is offshore-subsea or an onshore coastal easement are unconfirmed. Great-circle endpoint distance is ~170 km; a coast-hugging route of ~193 km (gem.wiki) is consistent. Coordinates are approximate, derived from named facilities — none fabricated.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints established from: Fluor (independent) confirming Safaniya-area gathered gas moves along the coast to Ju'aymah for processing; nsenergybusiness Safaniya field profile fixing the Safaniya field location (~260 km N of Dhahran, NW Arabian Gulf). Ju'aymah terminal coordinates are the well-known Ras Tanura-area terminal position. Coordinates approximate, defensible from named facilities; no coordinate invented. Exact onshore/offshore routing not sourceable → keep suggested accuracy low.
